title: audit-signal-taxonomy-and-operator-cheat-sheet
body:
Purpose and intent:
This is a compact working notes doc: a taxonomy of audit signals we should capture for customer-managed networking (VPC/on-prem), plus a short operator cheat-sheet for fast triage and approvals. The emphasis is pragmatic: signals that are "actionable + cheap to store" and sampling rules that keep latency-sensitive approvals moving while preserving forensic value.

Audience:
- Product PMs (private-deployments)
- SRE/Security oncall and operator teams
- Solutions engineers running customer handoffs

High-level problem statement:
Customers need to be able to prove who approved a VPC change, what changed, and when — without forcing us to store enormous raw packet captures or full configuration archives. We need a small set of canonical signals that satisfy auditors and allow post-incident reconstruction with high fidelity.

Principles (why these signals):
- Signal minimalism: store the smallest canonical artifact that proves intent and effect (signed approval + compact diff + evidence hash).
- Tiered retention: high-value proofs are kept longer; bulk telemetry is sampled aggressively.
- Latency first for approvals: any sampling/packing must not add >150ms median to the approval path.
- Privacy by default: redact PII from stored artifacts unless customer opts-in.

Signal taxonomy (recommended canonical set) - short names + rationale:
1) approval_receipt (primary)
   - What: time-stamped, operator/customer-signed JSON receipt (who, role, ticket id, policy rule matched, TTL).
   - Why: direct proof of consent. Keep full receipt for retention tier A.

2) compact_change_diff (primary)
   - What: semantically minimal delta (resource id, field, before/after hash) and human summary line. Not raw config.
   - Why: reconstruct patch intent; small and searchable.

3) evidence_manifest (primary)
   - What: pointers/hashes to related artifacts (syslog segments, siem ids) and a combined SHA256.
   - Why: integrity chaining for forensic reassembly.

4) approval_latency_metric (derived)
   - What: bucketed metric (ms) per approval request.
   - Why: alert on abnormal human-in-the-loop delays and detect automation failures.

5) operator_witness (secondary)
   - What: side-channel signals (operator CLI session id, operator ip, MFA factor used).
   - Why: correlation for suspicious patterns. Keep short-lived index.

6) network_flow_anchor (secondary, sampled)
   - What: compact flow metadata (connection tuples count, flow-start timestamp, flow-hash) near time-window of change.
   - Why: low-cost check that change produced expected traffic effect. Sampled at 1-5% by default.

7) rollback_trigger_token (derived)
   - What: precomputed quick-scan checksums that can be used to auto-generate a rollback bundle if thresholds exceeded.

Sampling & retention heuristics (practical):
- Tier A (retain 1 year): approval_receipt, compact_change_diff, evidence_manifest (for customer opted high-sensitivity or for incidents).
- Tier B (retain 90 days): approval_latency_metric, operator_witness indices (metadata only).
- Tier C (retain 14 days, sampled): network_flow_anchor at default 1% rate; increase sampling to 10% for first 24 hours after a change.
- Escalation: if any heuristic fires (latency > 10s, rollback_score > 0.7, suspicious operator ip), automatically persist Tier C artifacts for 7 additional days.

Packing rules (evidence-minimization):
- Never store raw credentials, ephemeral tokens, or full packet payloads.
- Replace PII with reversible encryption only if customer KMS consent is present.
- Use content-addressed storage: store hashes in evidence_manifest, blobs in cold storage when needed for investigations.

Operator cheat-sheet (quick triage sequence)
1) Before approving: check approval_policy -> does change match allowed policy? Quick CLI: `rictl policy check --ticket=PD-xxxx` (returns PASS/WARN/FAIL).
2) If WARN, open quick ticket template: `jira create PD-approval-warn --summary "WARN: <short>"` and notify customer slack thread with template below.
3) On approval, ensure receipt is signed: `rictl approval sign --ticket=PD-xxxx --operator=AishaR`. Verify SHA in console.
4) Post-change sampling boost: `opsctl sampling set --ticket PD-xxxx --window 24h --rate 10%` (temporary).
5) If latency anomaly: run `rictl approval inspect --since 1h --metrics latency` to fetch bucketed latency. If median > 5s, escalate to Eng oncall (ENG-SRE).

Quick Slack templates (copy/paste)
- Customer notification (pre-approval): "@customer-team Heads-up: change PD-xxxx scheduled. We'll keep 24h elevated sampling and retain proof artifacts for 14 days. Link: <console url>"
- Post-approval failure: "@eng-oncall PD-xxxx produced rollback_score 0.8; snapshot persisted in evidence bucket: s3://private-evidence/PD-xxxx. Please triage."

Suggested Jira labels and ticket fields
- labels: private-deploy, audit-evidence, sampling-boost
- custom fields: evidence_manifest_hash, approval_receipt_id, sampling_rate_at_change

Test cases (minimal coverage to ship):
- TC1: small config flip (ip route add) -> verify approval_receipt created and compact_change_diff contains a before hash.
- TC2: high-latency approval -> generated alert and Tier C artifacts persisted.
- TC3: PII redaction -> submit change with customer email in comment, verify stored receipt redacts email by default.

Open questions (for PD/Legal/Security):
- Default retention windows for customers in EU vs US (need legal signoff).
- KMS consent UX for reversible PII storage.
- Certifications: will auditors accept a hashed-change + manifest vs raw config? We should get a sample approval from 2 pilot customers.

Examples (toy JSON proof snippet)
{
  "approval_receipt_id": "AR-2025-0912-1394",
  "operator": "aisha.r@redwood",
  "ticket": "PD-3321",
  "timestamp": "2025-08-12T15:22:07Z",
  "policy": "vpc-minor-change-v1",
  "manifest_hash": "sha256:3b8f..."
}

Next steps (action items)
- Product: draft retention tiers per region and present to Legal by 2025-09-10. (Owner: Marco)
- Eng: implement lightweight approval_receipt schema and sign-by-default hook in control-plane. (Owner: Samir)
- SRE: add quick CLI commands to opsctl and document in runbooks. (Owner: Riley)

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep schema as small as possible; proofs should be human-readable first, machine-verifiable second.
- We should run a pilot with 2 enterprise customers and collect auditor feedback before setting Tier A default to 1 year.

References/links:
- Confluence sketch: confluence.company/internal/PD-evidence-taxonomy (see diagrams)
- JIRA PD-3321 (privacy/redaction epic)

End of cheat-sheet. This is a WIP: please add edge cases (multi-operator approvals, automated rollback vs manual) and pilot feedback inline.
